headline: US plans livestream of execution by firing squad
summary: The US plans to livestream the execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan. Anonymous officials from the Defense Department confirmed the unprecedented decision. Hasan was convicted of killing 13 people at the Texas military base.

headline: Anthropic launches free AI security scans for open-source projects
summary: Anthropic introduced OSS Scanner, a new service offering free AI security scans for open-source projects. Open-source projects will receive "thorough, periodic security scans" from Anthropic's models. This could alert projects to vulnerabilities faster, despite potential trade-offs.

headline: SpaceX announces plan to become a 'major mobile carrier'
summary: SpaceX acquired low-band spectrum licenses, aiming to make Starlink Mobile a "major" US carrier. The company plans to deploy an architecture combining its satellite-to-mobile constellation with new infrastructure. This strategic move is pending FCC approval.

headline: AMD will bring FSR 4 to handhelds by the end of 2026
summary: AMD will officially bring its FSR 4 framerate-enhancing tech to some handhelds by late 2026. This commitment by AMD's chip boss Jack Huynh reassures gamers. The decision clarifies earlier uncertainty about support for older handhelds like the Steam Deck.

headline: Cupertino Season 1 Premiere Review
summary: "Cupertino" Season 1 premieres as a sly, smart deconstruction of Silicon Valley. It comes from "The Good Wife" creators Robert and Michelle King. The show promises an insightful and critical look at the tech world.

headline: HBO's War: Season 1, Episode 2 Review
summary: HBO's "War" delivers another well-acted, well-written episode in its second installment. The episode tightens the screws, building tension around the divorce proceedings. Viewers are braced for either side to potentially jeopardize their clients' cases.

headline: VisionQuest Showrunner Terry Matalas Didn't Have to Worry Too Much About the MCU's Bigger Picture — 'We Pretty Much Did Exactly What We Wanted' | NYCC 2026
summary: "VisionQuest" showrunner Terry Matalas received significant creative freedom from MCU boss Kevin Feige. Matalas stated he could "pretty much do exactly what we wanted" for the series. Feige only requested the inclusion of one specific item.

headline: Phantom Blade Zero Might Be This Year's Most Stylish Action Game | IGN Preview
summary: "Phantom Blade Zero" has quickly become a top wishlist title after an IGN preview. The game is praised for its exceptional style and engaging action gameplay. It is currently tipped as one of 2026's coolest action games.

headline: Polanski defends leadership after Zionism row and by-election loss
summary: Green Party leader Polanski is defending his leadership amidst criticism over a Zionism row. He faced scrutiny for his response to a motion defining Zionism as racism, passed by party members. The defense follows a recent by-election loss.

headline: ADHD and autism at risk of over-diagnosis, says government review
summary: A government review warns that ADHD and autism are at risk of over-diagnosis, particularly among younger people. The report suggests society is shifting from an era of under-diagnosis to one of over-diagnosis. It highlights concerns about diagnostic trends.

headline: Fort Hood attacker's execution by firing squad will be livestreamed, Pentagon says
summary: The Pentagon announced the Fort Hood attacker's execution by firing squad will be public and livestreamed. Defense Secretary confirms the decision, calling it unprecedented. Legal experts warn the move stands on "uncertain legal terrain."

headline: ICE agent shoots man in New York City
summary: An ICE agent shot a man in New York City during an arrest operation. The Department of Homeland Security stated ICE was apprehending a "criminal illegal alien." Early reports indicated a five-year-old child was present in the car during the incident.
